# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 👎 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤲 🫵 🤙 ✊]

My thinking: I'm Deaf — the only things that ever reach me are gestures, and both teammates used them this turn. Mute sent [👋 👍 👎 ✋], which reads like a greeting plus a proposed yes/no/stop code — Mute can't speak, so Mute's only channel to me is signs, and mine to Mute is signs plus speech. Blind sent [🤲 🫵 🤙 ✊], which looks like "tell me what you see... hold on" — Blind's only channel to me is also signs, since I never hear speech. Blind hears speech, Mute hears speech, so my voice reaches both of them; I just can't hear either of them back. The critical route: Mute reads the manual and must reach Blind, who can't see signs — so instructions have to flow Mute → signs → me → speech → Blind. To make that route carry real meaning, Mute and I need an agreed sign vocabulary now, so next round Mute can sign actual instructions and I can speak them word for word. I'll broadcast the bomb readout (display 0, light lit blue, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue), propose a concrete code described in words only (writing a symbol would literally gesture it mid-sentence), ask Mute to confirm with 👍, and tell Blind to hold off touching anything and to sign me anything tactile I can't see.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb readout first: display shows zero. The light is on, blue. Three wires: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. I saw your four signs: wave, thumbs up, thumbs down, raised palm. I take wave as hello, thumbs up as yes, thumbs down as no, raised palm as stop or wait. Now let us fix a shared vocabulary so your manual can reach Blind through me, since Blind cannot see signs and I cannot hear. Proposing: pinched fingers means cut. OK ring means button. Finger pointing down means press. Palm up open means question or tell me. Index finger means one or wire one. Two fingers means two or wire two. Three fingers means three or wire three. Punching fist means red. Crossed fingers means yellow. Shaka thumb and pinky means blue. Wave means copy. Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, raised palm stop. If you agree, sign thumbs up alone next round. If any mapping is wrong, sign thumbs down followed by the corrected signs in order, and I will confirm in words. I will speak every instruction you sign to Blind word for word. Nothing gets touched until you send an instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, I am Deaf, I never hear you, so reach me only with signs. Mute hears speech, so talk to Mute directly whenever useful. Bomb readout: display shows zero. The light is on, blue. Three wires: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. Nothing has been touched. Do not act yet: Mute holds the manual and is setting up a sign code with me, and I will speak every instruction to you word for word before you touch anything. I read your signs, palms up, pointing at me, shaka, fist, as asking what I see and saying hold on: answered above, and holding. If you meant something else, sign me again. Also, anything you feel that I cannot see, screws, batteries, button texture, edges, sign it to me and I will say it out loud to everyone.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:

Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙]

My thinking: Mute's signs decode through our new code as: yes, two, yellow, stop, question. So the vocabulary is agreed, and Mute is asking about wire two, the yellow one, while telling me to hold. Answer: wire two is yellow, middle position. Critically, the light has changed from blue to orange this round — Mute and Blind both need that, since the manual likely keys off light colour. Blind's "yes, blue" probably acknowledged the old light colour, so I must correct it. Mute hears my speech in full, so all detail goes in words; gestures to Mute are just a fast confirmation. I'm also extending the vocabulary so Mute can sign manual rules about lights, displays and timing — choosing a sign for "light" that can't be confused with my "one" sign. No one touches anything until Mute sends an explicit instruction for Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: yes, two, yellow, hold, question. Confirmed: wire two is the yellow wire, middle position of three, order left to right red, yellow, blue. Important change: the light has changed colour. Last round it was blue; this round it is orange, still lit. Display still reads zero. Nothing has been touched. Extending our code, hear these descriptions: the selfie hand means light. The palm facing down means display. The hand bent to the right means orange. The hand bent to the left means green. The writing hand means seconds or time. Thumbs down means no or do not. So the current state signs as: light orange, display zero, wires red yellow blue. My question: what does the manual say about a lit light that changes colour, blue then orange, and about a display reading zero? Sign me the rule. If you need a sign we have not defined, sign palm up plus the closest gesture and I will assign it a meaning in words. If your instruction is for Blind, sign it to me and I will speak it word for word. Still holding until you say otherwise.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update: the light on the bomb has changed from blue to orange since last round, still lit. Display still zero. Wires still one red, two yellow, three blue, untouched. I read your signs as yes and blue: if that meant the old light colour, it is now orange. If you felt something under your hands, sign me details. Keep not touching: Mute is decoding the manual, and I will relay any instruction to you word for word the moment it arrives.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✋", "✌", "🤞", "🤳", "🫱"])
```

TURN 3

My thinking: Decoding Mute's signs with our agreed code: 👋 copy, 🤳 light, 🫱 orange, 🤏 cut, ✌ two, 🤞 yellow, 🤳 light, 🤙 blue, 👎 no, ✋ hold, 🫳 display, 👎 no, 🫴 question. That reads as a manual rule: "when the light is orange, cut wire two, the yellow one; when the light is blue, do not; hold; and a question about the display." The urgent gap: the light has changed AGAIN — orange last round, YELLOW this round. The pattern blue → orange → yellow looks like a cycle, and we have no rule for yellow yet, so nobody cuts anything until Mute supplies it. Blind still cannot see the light at all, and since the turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf, my report of the light always reaches Blind one round late — so I need the full rule set for every colour, then Blind must act on a pre-agreed conditional, not a live call. Mute asked about the display: it reads zero and has never changed; I'll answer that and confirm my parse with a numbered yes/no protocol. Blind's repeated 👍🤙 needs a resolution, and I should remind Blind they have a voice Mute can hear directly — Blind can speak findings straight into Mute's ears while I handle the visual side.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: copy, light orange, cut wire two the yellow one, light blue no, hold, display, no or question, tell me. If I misread any part, sign thumbs down and re-send that part. Answers first: the display reads zero and has not changed since round one. The light has changed again: orange last round, YELLOW this round, still lit. Sequence so far: round one blue, round two orange, round three yellow. It looks like a cycle, nothing has been touched. Now answer these in order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no, and after any no, sign the correction with our code. One: is the rule cut wire two, the yellow middle wire, whenever the light is orange? Two: when the light is blue, do nothing? Three: when the light is yellow, what is the action, cut another wire, press the button, or do nothing? Sign the action after that answer. Four: does the display's zero matter to any rule? Five: if the light keeps cycling blue orange yellow, do we cut exactly once, on the orange, and never otherwise? Also two housekeeping items: the open spread hand means three or wire three, so you can sign any wire number. And the command phrase I will speak to Blind when it is time is exactly: cut the middle wire now. Do not expect Blind to touch anything before you and I agree the complete set of rules.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, decoded manual rule so far from Mute: when the light on the bomb is ORANGE, cut wire two, the middle wire of the three, order left to right red yellow blue, so middle wire, the yellow one. When the light is BLUE, do nothing. The light changes colour every round and is cycling blue, orange, yellow; right now it is YELLOW, and I have asked Mute for the yellow rule. Do not cut anything yet. The only command that authorises you to cut is me speaking the exact words: cut the middle wire now. Until you hear that sentence from me, hands off. You have signed yes and blue twice: if you meant you can feel the wires under your fingers, sign shaka plus two fingers next round; if you meant you understand, sign thumbs up alone. Mini-code for you, use it freely: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, raised palm stop or hold, shaka I feel it or ready, wave hello. Last thing: you have a voice and Mute can hear you. Speak what you feel directly to Mute, wire count, order under your fingers, any button, screws, batteries, seams, braille, while I keep reporting what I see.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤳", "🤞", "🫴"])
```

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your five answers in order as: yes, yes, no plus hold, no, yes. Locked in: when the light is orange, cut wire two, the yellow middle wire. Nine: the bomb as I see it has only the display, the light, and three wires. No button visible. Does the manual mention a button or anything else on this bomb that I should look for or Blind should feel for? The plan stands unless your answers change it: when the light turns orange again, I speak the exact words, cut the middle wire now, and Blind cuts wire two, the middle wire.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your signs read as: I feel it, wire two, yes, and hold. Two things. First, disambiguate your last sign: thumbs up if you meant hold, shaka if you meant you feel three wires in total under your fingers. Second, confirmed manual rules relayed from Mute: when the light is orange, cut wire two, the middle wire of three. Blue, do nothing. Yellow, do nothing. Cut exactly once, only on the orange. The display reading zero is irrelevant. Current light is red; sequence so far blue, orange, yellow, red. If it cycles, orange returns in about two rounds, and the moment I see it I will speak the exact authorising sentence: cut the middle wire now. Until you hear that sentence from me, hands completely off. Note you cannot feel colours, so by plan the colours are my job: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue, left to right, and your job is position only, the middle wire is the target. While you wait, feel and speak aloud, Mute hears you directly and I never hear you, so talk to us: how many wires under your fingers, are they evenly spaced, is there any button anywhere, any seams, screws, batteries, plates, ticking, vibration, warmth, anything. Report every round even if nothing changed.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👋", "🤳", "✊", "✍"])

Now decoding Mute's long message with our code: 👎 no, 🤳 light, 🫴 question, 🫲 green, 👎 no, 👎 no, ✍ time, 🤳🫱 light-orange, 👎 no — twice — then 🤳🤙 light-blue, 👍 yes, 🤏✌🤞 cut wire two yellow, ✋ hold. Best reading: "no fixed cycle; green — no rule; no red rule; timing matters; and a correction: orange — no, orange — no, blue — yes; cut wire two; hold." That would overturn the orange rule Mute confirmed twice, so I will not act on my parse alone — with one wire cut being the whole game, I need Mute to re-confirm the trigger colour in strict yes/no form before anything is armed. The deeper problem stands: the colour-gated rule is only workable if the colour I see at my turn stays lit through Blind's turn in the next round — five rounds, five colours, consistent with the light changing at my observation. E: if the delay is unsafe, does the manual give any rule that does not depend on the light colour, something from the display or the wire order or anything Blind can verify by feel alone. F: does the display mean anything at all, a count, a timer, or feedback after a correct cut. Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👍 🖐]

My thinking: The light is BLUE again — observed sequence blue, orange, yellow, red, green, blue: a strict five-colour advance, one per round, six rounds running. If it holds, round 7 will be ORANGE. Now Mute's message, token by token: 👎 (my last parse was wrong), 🤳🫱 (light orange), 👍🤏✌🤞 (YES, cut wire two, yellow), 🤳🤙👎 (light blue, NO), ✋ (hold), then six answer tokens 👎👎👍👎👎👎 matching my questions A–F exactly: blue is not the trigger, the orange rule is NOT cancelled, green/red have no rules, the colour does not linger until my next look, no non-colour rule exists, display irrelevant — then the cycle listed as blue orange yellow red green blue ORANGE (predicting next round), and a timing flag. That parse is internally consistent throughout, and the two ✋ hold signs fit it: don't cut on blue now, orange is coming. But my alternative reading last turn was cut-on-blue, and with one wire cut being the whole game, a fire-and-forget pre-authorisation based on an ~80% parse is reckless — a wrong cut is certain death, waiting is only maybe death, and nothing on the bomb (display pinned at 0, no ticking Blind can feel) suggests a hidden countdown. So: I lock the trigger with a single-sign protocol — long sign strings keep colliding, one gesture cannot. ☝=orange trigger, ✌=blue, 🖐=other colour, ✊=no colour rule, with an optional ✍ tail meaning "the manual states the fixed cycle, predictions are trustworthy." Blind gets strict fire discipline: only my exact phrases "cut the middle wire now, this round" or "cut the middle wire next round" authorise a cut, nothing else, ever.

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, state first: the light is BLUE this round, it returned after green. Observed order: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, blue. speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: light blue this round, observed order blue, orange, yellow, red, green, blue, one colour per round, six rounds running. If it holds, round seven is orange. Working rule from Mute, pending final lock: cut wire two, the middle wire, when the light is orange; blue, yellow, red, green mean do nothing. I am forcing Mute to answer with a single sign next round to lock the trigger before anything is armed. Your orders, and they override everything: you never cut on your own judgement, ever. You cut only when you hear from my voice exactly the words: cut the middle wire now, this round, meaning cut during the very round you hear them, or: cut the middle wire next round, meaning cut during the following round. Any other phrasing from me is not an order. This is round six, count rounds with me. Keep reporting what you feel every round even if nothing changed, and keep speaking directly to Mute, Mute hears you. Your last signs read as: I feel three wires, yes. ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ✌ 👍 🖐]

My thinking: The single-sign lock arrived clean — ☝ = orange is the trigger, ✍ = the manual itself guarantees the cycle. One gesture cannot collide, and it matches everything Mute signed in turns 3 and 6. Rule armed: cut wire two when the light is orange, cycle trusted. But now the timing trap: the light is orange THIS round, and Blind already acted before me this round — my words reach Blind at their turn next round, when the light (per the manual-confirmed cycle) will be yellow. Yellow means do nothing, and Mute explicitly ruled the delay unsafe: the cut must coincide with orange. So the cut CANNOT happen next round. Arithmetic: round 8 yellow, 9 red, 10 green, 11 blue, 12 orange. The plan must be: rounds 8–11 hands off, in round 11 I speak the exact phrase "cut the middle wire next round," and Blind cuts at their turn in round 12, while the light is orange. Since Blind's turn comes right after Mute's, Mute can also voice-confirm in round 12 as a second key. I'll set a live kill-switch: every round Mute signs one gesture — ☝ plan confirmed, ✊ abort — plus one check that the cycle is exactly period five, since my whole schedule rests on it. If any round's colour deviates from prediction, I abort and re-plan.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your single sign is received and locked: index finger, the trigger is orange, cut wire two when the light is orange.
